pr_body:
As discussed in #11870:
Fix `X509_PUBKEY_cmp()`, move to crypto/x509/x_pubkey.c, export, and document it-
Solves #11870.
pr_comments: Nit: please add `Fixes #11870` to the body of the commit message.

Hmm... this number of different return values in different cases makes the semantics seriously convoluted. Especially for a function that is now being public. Is this function used for sorting? Does actually make sorting by pubkey any sense? If not, would it make sense to make the different return values just internal thing or collapse them (at least partially). Otherwise we might not be able to fulfil the API contract in future if we make some changes.
@t8m JFYI: it's partly discussed since there: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/11870#issuecomment-631504517

If we are only interested (in-)equality we should  return 1 for equal, 0 for non-equal, and < 0 on error and the function should not be called `*_cmp()` but `*_eq()`.

If we are interested in a comparison operation that assumes some order on the given datatype (even if it is just based on `memcmp()`) and can be used for building sorted container data types as done for `X509` we should return 1 for larger, 0 for equal, -1 for smaller, and < - 1 on error and the function should be named `_cmp()`.

In the improved version of `X509_PUBKEY_cmp()` a couple of days ago I tried to retain as much comparison information as possible, but the weird return value design of `EVP_PKEY_cmp()`, used to 'compare' public key data, results in the pretty awkward return values criticized above.

I'll try to find a proper and straightfordward solution such that `X509_PUBKEY_cmp()` is really a comparison operator in the above sense, like `X509_cmp` for instance.

Hmm.  X509_cmp is a rather bad example.
We should not follow it at all.
I think it should be fixed as well, since
actually it looks completely broken.
The only use that works is check for == 0 means equal.
-2 can also be the return value of memcmp !
here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/6e15b81c340e8124e45a92a2dbcd923c2ba4e79f/crypto/x509/x509_cmp.c#L145-L153

Note to myself: I must blame myself for trying to check the error of X509_check_purpose :-)

I meanwhile agree that the equality semantics makes more sense for `X509_PUBPKEY`, 
so I'll do that and consequently rename the function to `X509_PUBPKEY_eq()`.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged - thanks to all who contributed to the discussion on the best solution.
As the pull request is merged, it should be closed. I'd suggest adding the new API break to the already existing #9296 and we can call a vote on how it should be handled.

Good point @petrovr - it's a pity that `EVP_PKEY_cmp()` and `EVP_PKEY_cmp_parameters()` 
are not called  `EVP_PKEY_eq()` and `EVP_PKEY_eq_parameters()`, respectively.

This would avoid a lot confusion and would have avoided the bug found by @vt-alt.

Fix is now in #11894.

> Good point @petrovr - it's a pity that `EVP_PKEY_cmp()` and `EVP_PKEY_cmp_parameters()`
> are not called `EVP_PKEY_eq()` and `EVP_PKEY_eq_parameters()`, respectively.

Isn't it worth introducing these renaming here and now, altogether with deprecating the old ones as misleading?

> > Good point @petrovr - it's a pity that `EVP_PKEY_cmp()` and `EVP_PKEY_cmp_parameters()`
> > are not called `EVP_PKEY_eq()` and `EVP_PKEY_eq_parameters()`, respectively.

I fully agree and am willing to do that. 
How to do this best?
Can I rename for instance `EVP_PKEY_cmp()` to `EVP_PKEY_eq()` and add a `#define for backward compatibility?

> How to do this best?
> Can I rename for instance `EVP_PKEY_cmp()` to `EVP_PKEY_eq()` and add a `#define for backward compatibility?

If you do that the define should be within the `#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0`. Or you can even do `EVP_PKEY_cmp()` as a thin wrapper function - that has an advantage of producing deprecated warnings if used in the code.
We do currently not have any exported XXX_eq functions, right?
@t8m, done on #11953

> We do currently not have any exported XXX_eq functions, right?

Correct.

And how many of the currently expoerted _cmp functions return
-1 for "less" and +1 for "greater" ?

The point of the above discussed rename of `EVP_PKEY_cmp{,_parameters}` to `*_eq()` was to avoid in the future the confusion that lead to this bug report because there have been two different semantics for `*_cmp` functions: equality and order comparison.
Likely more functions are affected, such as the `EC_POINT_eq()` you just mentioned.
We could/should rename those as well, both for consistency and for avoiding the same confusion.

The proposed change does not force anyone to rename their function uses because this is handled by backward compatibility declarations.

The difference between EVP_PKEY_cmp and EC_POINT_cmp is that the first one returns 1 for equal where the second returns 0 for equal. So no, EC_POINT_cmp does not need to be renamed.

But there is also EVP_PKEY_cmp_parameters, which has the same semantics as EVP_PKEY_cmp and so it should be probably renamed as well.

But even X509_cmp is an exception, and in that case I made the mistake
to believe it is supposed to return -1, 0, +1 but instead it returns the result
of memcmp if it is non-zero, and that should be fixed as well.

> But there is also EVP_PKEY_cmp_parameters, which has the same semantics as EVP_PKEY_cmp and so it should be probably renamed as well.

#11953 already does that.

review_comments:
Do we consider this an API breaking change?

External applications will be required to change their source code, see this failure: https://travis-ci.org/github/romen/openssl/jobs/691216006

I am unsure if the fix is to update the gost engine to use the constified version (but this would also mean that sharing the codebase with 1.1.1 and 3.0.0-dev, this would require `#ifdef` guards) or to undo the constification.
Current gost-engine upstream is not compatible with 1.1.1 already

> Current gost-engine upstream is not compatible with 1.1.1 already

Ok, so this particular failure could be fixed by updating the gost source.

Yet, I want to raise the issue that any external app or engine that was using `EVP_PKEY_asn1_set_public()` will require a source change after the constification: it's not like we don't allow this for 3.0.0, but usually we have a conversation (if not a vote) about breaking API changes, and I don't think the matter was raised here.

It is perfectly acceptable to say that we will stick with the API change, I just want it to be acknowledged and approved explicitly.

Actually I don't understand what renaming X509_PUBKEY_cmp to X509_PUBKEY_eq
has to do at all with constification of pub_decode functions ?

This was needed  to allow 
`int X509_PUBKEY_eq(const X509_PUBKEY *a, const X509_PUBKEY *b)`
rather than
`int X509_PUBKEY_eq(X509_PUBKEY *a, X509_PUBKEY *b)`
and also independently of that function the constification should make much sense.
It's really a pity that for so many OpenSSL API functions `const` types for read-only parameters were not done right from the beginning.

> This was needed to allow
> `int X509_PUBKEY_eq(const X509_PUBKEY *a, const X509_PUBKEY *b)`
> rather than
> `int X509_PUBKEY_eq(X509_PUBKEY *a, X509_PUBKEY *b)`
> and also independently of that function the constification should make much sense.

I understand, and often constifying the arguments of a function do not cause source code compatibility issues!
But in this case, by changing the argument of a function pointer declaration we end up with a breaking API change.

I don't disagree with constification, and I wouldn't vote against the breaking change in this case, and I share the sentiment that it would have been better if it was const to begin with!

I just want to raise the issue that, as happened with the gost source, external applications will get failures out of this change and normally we require the reviewers to acknowledge and approve this, or even call a vote in some cases! 

> It's really a pity that for so many OpenSSL API functions `const` types for read-only parameters were not done right from the beginning.

Agreed!

How to deal with the API incompatibility here? Should there a voting?
Fortunately `EVP_PKEY_asn1_set_public()` is an 'expert-only' function.
Shall I document that API-breaking change, and how best to do that?

I just found that I missed to add the `const` in a further line of `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD.pod`:
```
 int (*pub_decode) (EVP_PKEY *pk, X509_PUBKEY *pub);
```

BTW strange that for `priv_decode()` and `param_decode()` the input parameter was already `const` but not for `pub_decode()`.

At the latest when documenting those functions in commit 751148e2b0d1048522d754d55319166435cdda86
the `const` issue introduced in commit 0f113f3ee4d should have been rectified.
Or could we just cast-away the const when the callback is called? I know, ugly and should be documented at least.

Again my question: How shall we proceed now with this (in my view minor) API incompatibility?
Is this something that we should decide/fix urgently before the release?
BTW, a week ago I realized that @mattcaswell had brought up a very similar issue 11  months ago, which is still open, too: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/9296
